llm._comment_budget_model: Explicit 3-level budget model (UK's specification): LEVEL perception_and_understanding (perception's own classification retry cascade PLUS semantic understanding's separate fallback -- these are two distinct sub-tasks sharing one level), LEVEL response_generation (cognition through Brain's final response), LEVEL post_response_reasoning (async self-evaluation/evolution after the reply is already sent). CORRECTED (2026-09-07): the override for perception_and_understanding was set to 3, but the real worst case at that level is perception's own primary+retry (2) PLUS semantic understanding's own primary+retry (2) = 4 -- the old cap of 3 meant that whenever perception itself struggled (used both its calls) AND semantic understanding needed its own retry too, the level was exhausted one call early and a genuine fact statement's extraction died with 'LLM per-level call budget exceeded' -- this is exactly the bug UK hit with 'wo hamirpur, UP me rahti h' failing to store. Raised to 4 to match the documented worst case. Note: the native symbolic-parser regex gap that caused THAT specific sentence to need the LLM fallback at all has separately been fixed in semantic_understanding/engine.py (rah-/reh- spelling + 'h' as short for 'hai') -- this budget fix is the defense-in-depth safety net for the remaining cases that genuinely do need the LLM. Typical turn: 1 call per level = 3 total (unchanged). Worst case is now 4+2+2=8.
llm._comment_max_output_tokens_per_turn: Worst case token spend at the 8-call ceiling across 3 levels: ~300 tokens x 8 calls + headroom for the 9th.
